issues.title: Missing Mozilla Public License header
issues.description: The rule requires that every .swift file begins with the exact Mozilla Public License header comment block at the top of the file. This file is missing the required header entirely.
issues.rule_name: All Swift Files Must Include Mozilla Public License Header

issues.title: Test completes without waiting for async image download
issues.description: The test was converted from async to synchronous but the expectation and wait statement were removed. This causes the test to complete immediately without waiting for the asynchronous image download callback to execute. The XCTAssert statements inside the completion handler will never be verified, resulting in false positive test passes even if the image download fails or produces incorrect results. This is a critical testing bug that undermines test reliability.

issues.title: Closure wrapper loses @Sendable annotation causing concurrency safety violation
issues.description: The moreButtonAction parameter is marked as @Sendable @MainActor to ensure thread-safe access in Swift 6 concurrency mode. However, the wrappedAction closure that wraps this action drops the @Sendable annotation, only keeping @MainActor. This breaks the sendability guarantee required by Swift 6, potentially allowing non-Sendable types to be captured and accessed from multiple threads unsafely. In Swift 6 strict concurrency mode, this will cause compiler errors or runtime crashes when the closure captures non-Sendable state.

issues.title: Async test assertion never verified due to missing expectation
issues.description: The test was updated to use @Sendable closures for Swift 6 concurrency compliance, but the expectation and wait statements were removed. The test now completes immediately without waiting for the asynchronous requestMediaCapturePermission callback. The XCTAssertEqual inside the decisionHandler closure will never execute, causing the test to always pass even when the media capture permission logic is broken. This is particularly problematic because this test validates critical permission handling behavior.

issues.title: Unsafe concurrency annotation on non-thread-safe static property
issues.description: The static generator property is marked with nonisolated(unsafe) despite the comment explicitly stating 'ContentBlockerGenerator is not thread safe'. This annotation bypasses Swift 6's concurrency safety checks and allows the non-thread-safe ContentBlockerGenerator to be accessed from multiple isolation domains without protection. This creates a potential data race condition where multiple threads could access the generator simultaneously, leading to undefined behavior, crashes, or data corruption. The unsafe annotation should only be used when the developer can guarantee thread safety through other means, which the comment explicitly contradicts.

issues.title: Static property missing explicit access control modifier
issues.description: Rule 11 requires explicit access control on properties/methods. The modified static property `generator` is declared without an explicit access modifier (e.g., `private`, `internal`, `public`).
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// FXIOS-14548 ContentBlockerGenerator is not thread safe
nonisolated(unsafe) static let generator = ContentBlockerGenerator.factory()
issues.rule_name: Rule 11: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

architecture.overview: BrowserKit is a local Swift package (BrowserKit/Package.swift) with shared modules such as WebEngine, SiteImageView, ComponentLibrary, and ContentBlockingGenerator. Each target sets its own swiftSettings, which previously enabled StrictConcurrency and RegionBasedIsolation as experimental flags and InferSendableFromCaptures as an upcoming flag. The PR moves the package to swift-tools-version 6.2, which makes Swift 6 language mode the default, so the per-target opt-in flags are removed. It also sets SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 on six ShareTo build configurations in firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj and adds Sendable adjustments in tests and in LabelButtonHeaderView.
steps: Start at BrowserKit/Package.swift. The tools version moves from 5.10 to 6.2, and each target drops its experimental and upcoming Swift flags.
Next, firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj sets SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 on six ShareTo configurations.
At runtime, LabelButtonHeaderView.configure wraps the optional @MainActor action in a non-optional closure before passing it to ActionButtonViewModel, which ActionButton.touchUpInside calls.
In tests, SVGImageProcessorTests drops async/await and the @MainActor on the GCDWebServer helper, and WKUIHandlerTests adds @Sendable annotations and removes an expectation that is no longer needed.
MainContentBlockerGenerator makes its static nonisolated(unsafe) and loses its MPL license header.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31468 - Refactor FXIOS-14466 FXIOS-14463 [Swift 6 Migration] Migrate ShareTo and BrowserKit Package to Swift 6

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves the BrowserKit package to Swift 6.2 tools and removes the StrictConcurrency, RegionBasedIsolation, and InferSendableFromCaptures opt-in flags from every target in Package.swift. It also sets SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0 on six ShareTo build configurations. The source changes are small: async/await is removed from the SVG image-processor tests, @Sendable annotations are added to test closures, nonisolated(unsafe) is applied to the content-blocker generator's static, and LabelButtonHeaderView wraps its optional action in a closure.

The Package.swift cleanup is mostly mechanical and consistent. The main problems are in the test edits: the standard SVG test now returns before its async assertions run, and the main-thread GCDWebServer guard was removed. The MPL license header was also deleted from one source file. CI is still pending, so the migration has not been shown to build.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The SVG test can pass without asserting anything, and the removed main-thread guard and license header should be restored. The Package.swift and WKUIHandler changes look sound, but CI has to confirm that ShareTo and the 6.2 tools bump build.

findings.title: SVG standard-case test no longer waits, so it can pass without asserting
findings.body:
The `testDownloadingSVGImage_withKingfisherProcessor_forStandardSVGCase` test removed its expectation and `wait`, but kept the `downloadImage` completion with its `XCTAssertEqual` calls. The download is asynchronous, so the test returns before the assertions run. The other download tests in the file keep their `wait`, so this one stands out. A test that can't fail gives false confidence.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift" lines="12-36"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift`, `testDownloadingSVGImage_withKingfisherProcessor_forStandardSVGCase` (around lines 12-36) calls `downloadImage` with a completion containing XCTAssert calls but has no expectation and no `wait`, so it returns before the callback runs. Add an `expectation(description:)` before the download, fulfill it in both branches of the completion, and call `wait(for: [exp], timeout: 2.0)` after the download. Match `testDownloadingSVGImage_withKingfisherProcessor_forSpecialSVGCase` in the same file.

findings.title: Main-thread GCDWebServer guard removed from mock server helper
findings.body:
The `startMockImageServer` helper lost its `@MainActor` annotation and the comment saying GCDWebServer must first be initialized on the main thread. That is a thread-affinity requirement, separate from actor isolation, so removing it as part of a Swift 6 cleanup drops the only protection for it. I haven't reproduced a crash, so treat this as a likely regression.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift" lines="207-209"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/SiteImageViewTests/SVGImageProcessorTests.swift`, `startMockImageServer` (around line 208) lost its `@MainActor` annotation and explanatory comment. Restore the main-thread guarantee for GCDWebServer initialization, either by putting `@MainActor` back on the helper or by making its containing extension `@MainActor`, and restore the original comment. Confirm the callers, which now drop `await`, still compile.

findings.title: MPL license header removed from MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift
findings.body:
The three-line Mozilla Public License header was deleted from this file. The other BrowserKit sources keep it, and the PR gives no reason for the removal. Header removals are easy to miss in review and can fail license checks.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift" lines="1-4"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift`, restore the three-line Mozilla Public License header at the top of the file, matching the other BrowserKit sources. Leave the `nonisolated(unsafe)` change and its FXIOS-14548 comment unchanged.

findings.title: Swift 6.2 tools bump is unverified and raises the toolchain requirement
findings.body:
Changing `swift-tools-version` from 5.10 to 6.2 requires a Swift 6.2 toolchain (Xcode 26 or later) for every developer and CI job that resolves this package. It also switches all BrowserKit targets to Swift 6 language mode. The PR relies on Bitrise to show the result, and the ShareTo change is only a `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` setting on six configurations with no source changes. Confirm the CI run passes and that every ShareTo configuration has the setting.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Package.swift" lines="1-1"}
findings.fixPrompt: Confirm that the CI toolchain and local developer setup support Swift 6.2 before the `swift-tools-version: 6.2` bump in `BrowserKit/Package.swift` is merged. Also confirm that `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` in `firefox-ios/Client.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` is set for every ShareTo build configuration. Report the Bitrise build and test results for ShareTo and the BrowserKit package.

findings.title: Unnecessary closure wrapper in LabelButtonHeaderView
findings.body:
`wrappedAction` only forwards to `moreButtonAction?`. Behavior is unchanged, but it allocates a closure on every configure call. If the wrapper exists only to satisfy the type checker, passing `moreButtonAction` directly may compile.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Home/Homepage/SectionHeader/LabelButtonHeaderView.swift" lines="104-112"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Client/Frontend/Home/Homepage/SectionHeader/LabelButtonHeaderView.swift`, `configure` (around lines 104-112) wraps `moreButtonAction` in `wrappedAction` before creating `ActionButtonViewModel`. Try passing `moreButtonAction` directly as `touchUpAction` and removing the wrapper. If the compiler rejects it under Swift 6 mode, keep the wrapper and add a comment explaining why.

findings.title: nonisolated(unsafe) hides a known thread-safety issue
findings.body:
The `generator` static is marked `nonisolated(unsafe)`, which turns off the compiler's concurrency check. The FXIOS-14548 comment says `ContentBlockerGenerator` is not thread-safe. This is safe today only because `main()` is the sole caller, and nothing stops a future caller from sharing the instance across threads.

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift" lines="5-6"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Sources/ExecutableContentBlockingGenerator/MainContentBlockerGenerator.swift`, `generator` (around line 6) is marked `nonisolated(unsafe)` with a FXIOS-14548 comment. Extend the comment to state that only `main()` uses this instance and that sharing it across threads is unsafe. Confirm FXIOS-14548 is tracked.

findings.title: Media-capture test change is correct
findings.body: `WKUIHandler.requestMediaCapturePermission` calls `decisionHandler` synchronously on both branches, so `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` can assert inside the closure without an expectation. The `@Sendable` annotations match the `@MainActor` decision-handler parameter.

findings.title: Experimental Swift flag cleanup in Package.swift is consistent
findings.body: Under the 6.2 tools version, `StrictConcurrency`, `RegionBasedIsolation`, and `InferSendableFromCaptures` are part of the default Swift 6 mode, so removing them from every target makes the package read more clearly. The leftover empty `swiftSettings` arrays are cosmetic.
